# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Dwarf bamboo (*Sasa* spp.) is expanding into Japanese alpine snowbed vegetation, excluding subordinate species and threatening plant diversity. Mapping its distributional change requires approximately 1 m resolution, because alpine vegetation forms a fine mosaic along microtopographic gradients. Using 10 years of ground-based time-lapse imagery of an alpine slope on Mt. Tateyama, Japan, we produced 1 m vegetation maps for 2012 and 2021 and per-pixel snowmelt dates for 2011–2021. Over 9 years, *Sasa* showed a net change of +19% (gross expansion 48%, gross loss 29%, nearly half of it exchange with dwarf pine). Because *Sasa* expands through both rhizome elongation and seed dispersal, we fitted two models under a common spatial-block design: a habitat suitability model of where conditions permit *Sasa* (Model A) and an establishment model of the observed 2012→2021 transitions, including distance from the existing front (Model B). In both models, snowmelt climatology (the 2011–2021 mean snowmelt date) was among the strongest environmental predictors and indicated a favourable snowmelt window (day of year approximately 150–185). Establishment probability over 9 years, however, was most strongly associated with proximity to existing patches: approximately 10% within 5 m of the front and below 1% beyond 10 m. Environmentally suitable area exceeded occupied area approximately 16-fold, suggesting that dispersal constrains the current distribution more than environment. A stochastic cellular automaton using Model B reproduced the observed expansion and projected approximately 4,900 m² of new establishment by 2030 under unchanged snowmelt and 5,700 m² under continuation of the observed, statistically undetectable trend; these are scenarios, not forecasts. Nine tenths of expected establishment within herbaceous vegetation fell in two snowbed communities adjoining existing patches. Near-term expansion is therefore spatially predictable, making removal or containment at fronts bordering snowbeds a high-priority candidate intervention, complemented by surveillance of environmentally suitable areas for establishment from seed.

# Data Availability Statement {.unnumbered}

The imagery-derived vegetation and snowmelt rasters, terrain predictors, all fitted model objects, projection outputs, and scripted analysis pipeline with its acceptance tests are permanently archived at Zenodo (<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22745234>). A development mirror is maintained at <https://github.com/0kam/SasaSDMPaper>.
